messages:
maya (PM): Quick sync — I pushed a first-pass PRD for Dedicated Capacity SLA + Autoscale. Need focused review on: acceptance criteria, sizing assumptions, and edge-case behavior for rollbacks.

jon (Eng): Reading now. top-level question: are we targetting p95 or p99 for SLA? customers ask for p99 but that drives significantly more idle capacity.

maya (PM): Customer asks are p99 for latency and 99.9% availability for committed throughput. Proposal in doc: p95 latency target for standard tier, p99 for enterprise reserved pools. Want feedback on feasibility + rollout plan.

sam (SRE): We should quantify latency by request size. For regen-style traffic p99 of full requests isn't meaningful. Suggest metric: p99 request latency for requests <= 512 tokens and separate bucket for >512.

leila (Infra Eng): Agree with sam. Also need to call out cold-start window. Dedicated warm pool should guarantee capacity to meet committed TPS within X seconds. Doc currently says "warm pool" but no SLO. Recommend: 60s to reach committed throughput after a sustained burst, otherwise failover to best-effort tier.

maya (PM): Good. Proposed explicit acceptance criteria to add: 
- Committed throughput delivered 95% of the time within 60s of sustained customer traffic spike (sustained = 30s).
- p99 latency for <=512 tokens under committed throughput <= 220ms.
- Availability for committed endpoints >= 99.9% over a 30d window.

jon (Eng): 220ms p99 is tight on some GPUs depending on model variant and batching. We should make latency target model-dependent and add a table. e.g., for Llama2-70B-qlora quantized we expect p99 ~300ms. Keep enterprise SLA but allow model-profiled SLOs.

ellie (CS): From customer side, they want deterministic SLAs in contract. They're okay if SLA differs by chosen model as long as contract shows expected numbers. Need clear language for sales.

aaron (Product Ops): We also need acceptance criteria for autoscale: when traffic exceeds commit, autoscale should add burst capacity within 45s and cap at N extra GPUs. Also define cost fallback policy (throttle vs route to hosted).

leila (Infra Eng): Autoscale hysteresis: scale-up if CPU/GPU queue sustained > 70% for 30s; scale-down only after 5m below 40% to avoid flapping. Document should include these numbers.

sam (SRE): Edge case: cross-region failover when a region loses capacity. Need a graceful degradation plan: route to secondary region with a downgraded model variant and notify customer with an SLA credit trigger. Also record sawtooth workload that rapidly oscillates — ensure autoscale doesn't overshoot.

jon (Eng): Adding a small config snippet to PRD suggestion:
```
autoscale_policy: 
  scale_up_threshold: 0.7  # queue occupancy
  scale_up_duration: 30s
  scale_down_threshold: 0.4
  scale_down_duration: 300s
  max_burst_gpus: 4
  warm_pool_min: 1
```

maya (PM): Nice. Include that. Also need an explicit rollout acceptance test. Proposed canary: 5% of traffic for 24h -> increase to 25% for 48h -> full. Measure p99 latency, error rate, and cost deviation against baseline.

ellie (CS): For customers on contracts, canary traffic should exclude their production endpoints unless they opt-in. We must make opt-in explicit in legal.

aaron (Product Ops): Acceptance checklist item: create post-deploy canary dashboard covering p50/p95/p99 latency (by token bucket), committed throughput delta, failover count, and warm-pool fill-time metric.

sam (SRE): Add runbook snippet for partial failure:
- detection: >3% request-errors in 5m or p99 latency degradation >2x baseline
- mitigation: route to secondary region with fallback model; reduce concurrency and bump batching to temporary higher latency target
- escalation: page on-call if mitigation > 10m

leila (Infra Eng): Edge-case: shorter request TTL on client side causes long tails to become errors during failover. Document should require instrumenting client SDKs to retry with exponential backoff and a 10s overall deadline for interactive requests.

jon (Eng): Another engineering constraint: we need pinned model variants for SLA endpoints. If a newer model is rolled out, it must be explicitly promoted; automatic model upgrades can't happen for committed pools. That should be acceptance criteria.

maya (PM): Good call. I'll add: "No automatic model upgrades for committed endpoints; explicit change control and customer notification 7 days prior."

ellie (CS): Customers will ask for credits if we fail their committed throughput. Define credit formula: (minutes of missed committed throughput / total minutes in billing period) * monthly commit * credit rate. Keep simple.

aaron (Product Ops): We'll draft formula in SLO appendix. Also need definition for "missed committed throughput" — use per-5m windows where delivered throughput < 90% of commit.

maya (PM): Next steps: I'll update PRD with these items and ping for a final review tomorrow. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we'll lock acceptance criteria and start engineering implementation planning.

jon (Eng): Quick note: add a dev task to run stress tests on Llama2-70B and Llama1-13B profiles to populate model SLO table.

sam (SRE): +1. I'll add the runbook PR and test harness for warm-pool fill-time.

deploy-bot: deployed docs/dedicated_capacity/PRD_v0.3 -> staging :white_check_mark:

maya (PM): Thanks everyone — this is shaping up. I'll push updated PRD and ping channel when ready. :rocket:
